svg.title: Chordrift database v2 schema overview
svg.desc: Conceptual organization of Chordrift database v2 tables and the lifecycle of a track manually removed from Spotify.
svg.text: Chordrift database v2 — conceptual Neon table map
Clean v0.1.4 runtime after migration 0044 cleanup and 0045 hardening. Tables are grouped by responsibility, not alphabetically.
One current inventory; unchanged bodies are reused
What should happen, independent of today’s Spotify state

g.text: Review evidence, Re-evaluate queue, account policy

svg.text: Typed recipe facts; raw ZIPs remain outside PostgreSQL

g.text: Display metadata stored once per historical provider track
May resolve lazily to a canonical track

svg.text: Plans, approvals, applies, and verification — without embedding whole inventories
Versioned caches; eligible for retention policies
7 · Clean runtime staging and external recovery boundary
Legacy physical tables are gone. Transient imports empty at commit; verified dumps and raw provider archives remain outside Neon.

g.text: Transaction-local staging; verified empty after every committed pull
verified logical dump · immutable Spotify ZIPs
Never embedded in a shipped client
Lightweight pull receipts and durable provider-external audit remain in Neon
V0.2 product tables extend this clean foundation additively

svg.text: Example · you manually remove a song from a managed Spotify playlist
Chordrift records observed state first. It does not erase history or silently invent intent.

g.text: A later pull proves the approved outcome.
Excluded tracks are not silently restored.

svg.text: Arrows show major ownership/dataflow links, not every foreign key. The v0.1.4 runtime is v2-only; raw Spotify ZIPs and the verified recovery dump remain outside Neon.
